ai.description: *Raorchestes griet* is a small shrub frog (20–25 mm) with a brownish-grey dorsum and dark, irregular mottling. It features a distinct white throat and granular skin on its belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Raorchestes griet* by the distinct, dark-edged, cream-colored "X" or hourglass-shaped marking on its back, which is absent in most similar bush frogs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes griet* inhabits the high-altitude shola forests and adjacent grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Griet Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of high-altitude shola forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes griet* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of eggs in leaf litter during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: The Griet Bush Frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, specifically occurring in the high-elevation shola forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Griet Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" notes, typically heard calling from dense vegetation within high-altitude shola forests.
